title: Feedback loomed dossier — runtime & product asks (Jun 2027)
content:
Summary:
This is a working compilation of customer feedback gathered between 2027-05-20 and 2027-06-08 from frontline CS calls, NPS follow-ups, and two on-site sessions. Purpose: surface repeat asks that meaningfully affect cost or reliability economics, map to likely engineering surface, and propose small, testable probes we can run in the next 6 weeks.

High-level themes (ranked by frequency + impact):
1) Token / per-request cost transparency (esp. around embeddings + streaming): customers want per-route and per-token breakout visible in the console + API responses for billing reconciliation. Several customers reported surprise when embedding-heavy pipelines spiked monthly bills.
2) KV-cache visibility & control: requests for cache hit metrics by key prefix, TTL diagnostics, and a manual "warm cache" helper for cold-start heavy workloads. Many ask threads tie this to latency tail issues.
3) Safer rollouts & fallback visibility: customers using Dedicated want clearer guarantees on fallback model variants (which exact quantized model was used when capacity constraints triggered), and a way to label fallbacks for A/B analysis.
4) Private onboarding friction: the VPC-instantiation checklist has unknown timing for customers; they'd like a live ETA and a lightweight diagnostic bundle to hand to infra teams.
5) Longer telemetry retention and per-request debug ids: enterprise customers want 90–180d retention for request traces and a stable request id that persists across retries and fallbacks.

Representative quotes (verbatim / annotated):
- "We saw embeddings cost jump 3x in one week and couldn't backfill which calls caused it." — finance lead, FinData (mid-market) 2027-05-27
- "When the cache is cold our latency goes from 200ms to 1.2s; hard to explain to product folks." — eng manager, Converso (AI startup) 2027-05-31
- "We need a version tag when fallback happens; today it just says 'fallback' and we lose signal." — platform eng, HealthSync (enterprise) 2027-06-03

Feature requests (concrete items) with rough impact + effort notes: 
A. Per-route token / cost attribution in console + export (CSV) — Impact: high (reduces billing disputes). Effort: medium. Accept criteria: CSV export with per-route token counts, UI drilldown for top 20 routes over 30/90 day window. Linked ticket: CS-2417.

B. KV-cache diagnostics page + API: surface hit rate by prefix, top miss prefixes, and ability to prewarm keys via API call — Impact: medium-high for latency-sensitive apps. Effort: medium (runtime + small UI). Quick probe: add cache-miss logging for 2 pilot customers for 2 weeks (low-effort) to validate signal.

C. Rollout/fallback transparency: augment response metadata with fallback_reason and model_variant_id; add console timeline showing fallback events per rollout — Impact: high for Dedicated/Private customers. Effort: medium-high (policy + telemetry plumbing). Linked ticket: ENG-1423.

D. Private deployment onboarding checklist + "air-gap bundle" generator (automated diagnostic script) — Impact: medium. Effort: small (docs + one-off script). Acceptance criteria: < 1 hour checklist that customers can run to collect logs and certs, returning a single tarball for Redwood SRE to inspect.

E. Retain request traces 90 days for enterprise plans, expose stable-request-id in API responses — Impact: medium. Effort: medium (storage + privacy review). Risk: PII retention; must go through compliance.

Operational quick wins (can be shipped as experiments):
- Add a lightweight per-request header (X-RW-TRACE-ID) in hosted responses for 2 weeks on opt-in beta so CS can reconcile tickets.
- Add a UI badge for routes with >50% streaming tokens to highlight embedding-heavy cost drivers.
- Pilot cache-miss telemetry with two customers (Converso + RetailX) and share daily heatmap CSVs with their eng leads.

Customer segmentation notes (who asked what):
- Startups / AI-native: care most about latency tail and cost predictability (KV cache, warmers, per-request headers). More willing to run probes.
- Mid-market SaaS: want billing reconciliation and per-route exports; less appetite for enabling beta headers unless doc'd.
- Enterprise (health/finance): longer telemetry + private onboarding; require compliance signoff for retention features.

Open questions / unresolved points:
- Storage cost model for 90d trace retention: do we add a surcharge or fold into enterprise SLA? Need finance input.
- Prewarm API semantics: should prewarm be an async hint to runtime or a hard guarantee for reserved memory? (affects runtime complexity)
- Fallback labeling: do we encode numeric variant ids only, or human-readable tags + commit hashes? (tradeoff: clarity vs. churn)

Risks and potential mitigations:
- Telemetry retention & compliance: mitigate by creating PII redaction step and a phased opt-in for enterprise tenants only.
- Runtime impact of prewarm: start with simulated warmers in Dedicated only; measure mem/cpu impact for 2 weeks.

Proposed next steps (6-week plan):
Week 1: share this draft with Eng runtime + Product (meeting 6/18). Spin up CS pilot list (Converso, FinData, HealthSync, RetailX). Create tickets: CS-2417 assigned, ENG-1423 triaged.
Week 2–3: implement opt-in X-RW-TRACE-ID header and per-route CSV exporter MVP; begin cache-miss telemetry pilot.
Week 4: review pilot data, refine acceptance criteria. Product to scope UI work for cost-export and fallback timeline.
Week 5–6: ship per-route CSV MVP and rollout fallback metadata in beta for Dedicated; produce "private onboarding" diagnostic script.

Notes to self / meeting prep bullets for 6/18 sync:
- Bring concrete pilot customer list and ask for Eng runtime lead time estimate for cache-miss telemetry and fallback metadata (approx hours).
- Finance: need quick model for storage surcharge for 90d retention (ballpark $/tenant/month).
- Legal/Compliance: quick checklist for PII in traces (who signs) and required redaction.

Attachments / raw sources used to compile this doc:
- CS call notes May 20–31 (internal docs)
- Post-call NPS follow-ups (FinData, Converso)
- On-site interview transcript (HealthSync 2027-05-28)

Quick TL;DR we can send to execs: 
- Top 3 asks: cost transparency per-route, KV-cache diagnostics, and fallback visibility.
- Low-friction probes: trace-id header, cache-miss telemetry pilot, CSV export MVP.
- Biggest blocker: compliance question on telemetry retention.

Unresolved: awaiting Eng/Finance/Legal inputs (list below).
